prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core promise
- “Get Brexit Done”: Pass the negotiated deal immediately, leave the EU in January 2020, negotiate an FTA in 2020, no extension beyond December 2020. Leave the single market/customs union and end ECJ jurisdiction while maintaining high standards on workers’, consumer and environmental protections.
- Fiscal approach: No borrowing for day-to-day spending; invest up to 3% of GDP in public net investment; keep debt falling; reassess if debt interest hits 6% of revenue.
- Tax guarantees: No rises in income tax, National Insurance or VAT rates. Raise NI threshold to £9,500 (ambition: first £12,500 tax-free).

Public services and cost of living
- NHS: Record funding settlement; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50m more GP appointments; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health law reform; clamp down on health tourism; NHS not on the table in trade talks; free hospital parking for those in greatest need.
- Social care: Cross-party long-term reform; £1bn extra each year; guarantee no one forced to sell their home; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.
- Education: £14bn extra over three years; per-pupil minimums; teacher starting salary to £30k; Ofsted retained; behaviour and exclusions backed; SEND funding boost; arts premium; PE investment.
- Families and welfare: £1bn for wraparound childcare; keep pension triple lock, bus pass and winter fuel; end benefit freeze; improve Universal Credit (main carer focus); reduce disability reassessments; tackle pension “net pay” anomaly.

Crime, justice and security
- 20,000 more police; Police Covenant in law; more stop and search (fair/proportionate); tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole-life for child murder); 10,000 more prison places; parole reform; national cyber crime force and National Crime Lab; stronger NCA; online harms legislation; Victims’ Law; domestic abuse support.
- Immigration: Australian-style points system; overall numbers down; fast-track NHS visa; equal EU/non‑EU treatment; 5-year qualification for benefits; increase NHS surcharge; Windrush compensation.

Economy, business and skills
- Business: Fundamental rates review; immediate relief for retail, pubs, small cinemas, music venues; late payments clampdown; expand start-up loans; R&D tax credit to 13% and broadened to data/cloud; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief; support self-employed.
- Skills: £3bn National Skills Fund; more apprenticeships, tied to major projects; upgrade FE estate; 20 Institutes of Technology; £500m of Shared Prosperity Fund for disadvantaged people’s skills.

Infrastructure, housing and local renewal
- Transport: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub; roads investment; EV rapid-charging network (£1bn); restore Beeching lines; superbus networks; cycling fund; contactless ticketing expansion; HS2 decision post‑review; minimum service during strikes.
- Digital: Gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard-to-reach areas.
- Towns/culture: £3.6bn Towns Fund; £150m Community Ownership Fund; £250m Cultural Investment Fund; safety/CCTV funding.
- Housing: Target 300k homes/year; “infrastructure first”; design codes; building safety post‑Grenfell; protect/enhance Green Belt; shared ownership reform; renters’ “no fault” eviction ban and single lifetime deposit; extend Help to Buy to 2023; stamp duty surcharge for non‑UK residents; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament.

Environment and rural
- Net Zero by 2050; 40GW offshore wind by 2030; £800m for first CCUS cluster; hydrogen and nuclear support; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; £4bn for flood defences; EV transition consultation; fracking moratorium.
- Nature: Office for Environmental Protection; £640m Nature for Climate Fund (75k acres trees/year) and peatland restoration; plastics levy, extended producer responsibility, deposit return scheme; ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD.
- Farming and fishing: Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; maintain farm budgets this Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme; leave CFP, sustainable fisheries and coastal regeneration.
- Animal welfare: Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long-distance live transport; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; tackle cat theft.

Union, democracy and global Britain
- Strengthen the Union; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum; Shared Prosperity Fund to at least match EU funds; English devolution white paper; up to 10 freeports.
- Democracy: Repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; voter ID; fair boundaries; defend free speech (no Leveson 2; repeal s40); Constitution, Democracy & Rights Commission; update JR/HRA balance.
- Defence/foreign: Exceed 2% of GDP (+0.5% real growth); modernise forces (Space Command), maintain Trident; veterans’ protections and support; 0.7% aid maintained; Magnitsky sanctions; target FTAs covering 80% of UK trade in three years (US, AUS, NZ, Japan), uphold standards; NHS not in trade deals.
